title: 對不起，我愛上了別人的女朋友。這將是我最後一次使用禁忌之力丨約會丨把妹丨情感丨戀愛丨約炮丨男性自我提升丨短期關係丨長期關係丨dating in china

timeline.summary: Mikey previews a later pregnancy/paternity conversation, says he regrets using what he calls a forbidden power, says another man was harmed, and states he did not initially know the woman had a boyfriend.

He recounts noticing that the woman liked a dog post, selectively messaging her, and interpreting her initially sparse replies. He teaches that engagement with one's posts can be a warmer lead, then describes challenging rather than continually supplying topics when she sent only reactions.

He reads later chat exchanges as increasing investment, stresses not appearing urgent, describes playful and sometimes confrontational replies, and uses their exchange about location and meeting to illustrate his idea of emotional resonance and behaving without fear that the topic will die.

The exchange moves to voice messages and a phone call. He explains his escalation from voice notes to calling, describes joking that ignores status displays, and frames this as remaining unaffected rather than matching the other person's self-presentation.

He says a 361-minute call changed the interaction. In the account, the woman discloses that she has had a boyfriend for four years, after which Mikey says he hesitated but continued. The video begins playing edited call material mixed with his live commentary.

In the played material, the woman is presented as saying she normally dislikes male attention but experiences this conversation differently and has an impulse to meet. Mikey repeatedly interprets these statements as attraction and uses hypothetical past-life/relationship language to intensify intimacy.

Mikey labels his method as push-pull or playing hard to get: he says that after the woman expresses a wish to meet but faces constraints, he outwardly reduces urgency while continuing to seed a romantic scenario. He explicitly says he did not disparage her boyfriend, but also rationalizes continuing despite the existing relationship.

He shows a move to a smaller account and says the pair used affectionate language, exchanged a song and had another long call. The discussion turns from flirting to concrete arrangements for an in-person meeting.

The edited call discusses several plans for the woman to travel while concealing the real purpose from her boyfriend and family, including using a female friend as cover, routing through Shenzhen, or claiming the friend had business in Chengdu. Later messages indicate that she unexpectedly booked a flight and asked Mikey to meet her at Tianfu airport.

Mikey says they met and plays more alleged in-person audio containing sexual and pregnancy/paternity hypotheticals. He then generalizes the case into claims about women accepting harmful conduct from a man they strongly desire.

He closes with a promotional pitch. He says he teaches the underlying ability but does not want students to repeat this conduct, and frames the lesson as avoiding the role he calls a provider in favor of a lover role.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: On social media, people who have already engaged with one of your posts are warmer prospects than complete strangers, so he selectively messages from that group.
claims.conditions: His personal TikTok practice and this single case; it is not a measured response-rate study and does not imply entitlement to a reply.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: When the other person gives low-effort replies, he recommends not anxiously carrying the whole conversation; he instead names the low investment, challenges playfully, then withdraws.
claims.conditions: The boundary between playful challenge and unwanted pressure depends on receptivity. Silence, refusal, hostility or discomfort must end the attempt; this upload does not supply a reliable decision rule.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He interprets conversational strength as speaking freely without fear that every topic must land, and as not changing one's behavior merely because the other person signals status or value.
claims.conditions: A self-presentation claim illustrated by his own banter; it should not be used to excuse ignoring explicit boundaries or demeaning the other person.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: Mutual voice-note exchange can be used as a signal that proposing a phone call may be timely, rather than escalating only because one party sent a single voice message.
claims.conditions: A low-stakes invitation only; acceptance must be explicit and either person can decline or end the call.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He presents the first long call as the point where attraction and disclosure increased, but says he learned only during that call that she already had a boyfriend.
claims.conditions: Self-reported chronology supported by edited chat/call displays, not an independently verified complete conversation record.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: After the woman expressed an impulse to meet but described practical obstacles, he says he reduced visible urgency while continuing to plant romantic imagery; he explicitly labels this push-pull and part of his forbidden method.
claims.conditions: This is a description of manipulative conduct in an infidelity context. It must not be converted into action advice.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says disparaging the existing boyfriend would be low value, yet he continues the romantic pursuit and rationalizes it by putting impulse or nature before social morality.
claims.conditions: The video itself includes regret and a promise not to repeat the conduct. Preserve the contradiction rather than extracting a recommended technique.

claims.speaker: Mikey and a woman presented in edited call material
claims.statement: The video records several plans for concealing the true travel purpose from the woman's boyfriend and family so she could meet Mikey in Chengdu.
claims.conditions: Third-party and played-material attribution is only partly recoverable from automatic transcription. The plans involve deception and must remain descriptive evidence, never advice.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He interprets the woman's reluctance to marry her boyfriend and willingness to travel as evidence that women prefer a man they experience as strongly desirable over a devoted provider.
claims.conditions: A sweeping gender and evolutionary claim inferred from one self-reported case; no independent evidence supports the generalization.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: At both the opening and closing, he says he regrets harming the boyfriend, did not initially know of the relationship, and does not want students to repeat this conduct even though he markets the underlying capability.
claims.conditions: This disclaimer does not erase the detailed demonstration or promotional framing, so the source remains restricted.

examples.summary: A like on a dog post becomes the opening for a TikTok private message; the early replies are sparse and Mikey alternates short playful messages with leaving the conversation alone.
Voice-note reciprocity leads to a proposed call; the screenshot shown at about 17 minutes displays a 361:49 voice call, while the narration says the boyfriend disclosure occurred during that call.
The edited phone material moves from hypothetical romance to three concealment plans for travel, followed by messages about a Tianfu airport arrival and an asserted in-person meeting.
The final played audio contains pregnancy and paternity hypotheticals; Mikey uses it to make a broad claim about desire overriding a partner's good treatment.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Mikey
speaker_attribution.basis: Visible on-camera host throughout the sampled frames. His live narration, retrospective explanation and sales pitch are directly attributable to him.

speaker_attribution.speaker: woman in the case
speaker_attribution.basis: Represented through anonymized chat screenshots and edited call/in-person recordings. Some alternating lines can be inferred from Mikey's narration, but the automatic transcript has no speaker labels and her identity and consent to publication are not verified.

speaker_attribution.speaker: the woman's boyfriend
speaker_attribution.basis: Never directly heard or shown in the reviewed evidence; all information about him is reported by Mikey or attributed to the woman.

speaker_attribution.speaker: livestream viewers and quoted/inserted media
speaker_attribution.basis: Viewer comments and illustrative inserts appear on screen. They are not Mikey claims and are excluded from the distilled claims unless he explicitly adopts them.

visual_findings: All 54 sampled frames were reviewed. The dominant layout is Mikey on camera beside enlarged private-message screenshots, with a livestream chat column and a promotional overlay.

The right side shows a chronological but edited selection of TikTok/other chat messages, voice notes, call-duration cards and later WeChat messages. It is not a complete raw export, so omitted messages and exact continuity cannot be established.

Frame 24 visibly shows a 361:49 voice call; frames 43 and 46 show a later 421:58 call card; frames 51-52 show later itinerary/airport-style exchanges. These support the coarse sequence but not the truth of the underlying relationship claims.

Names and avatars are blurred in many screenshots, but a cutout photo of the woman is repeatedly used and contextual details remain visible. Privacy, consent-to-publication and third-party exposure require separate review.

The 45-second sampling is sparse. Reopening key sampled JPGs at their stored 960x540 resolution improved legibility of call durations and coarse message order but did not provide continuous audio-visual verification.

permissions.reason: The upload centers on infidelity, concealment, manipulation, private communications, unverified third-party facts and unsupported gender generalizations. It also may be an edited excerpt of EPmR6XOphxY. Only descriptive, attributed research use is currently permitted.

limitations: The transcript is automatic and was read in full, but it was not checked word-for-word against the original audio; several words and pronouns are plainly mistranscribed.
Played calls and in-person recordings are interleaved with Mikey's commentary without speaker labels, so fine-grained attribution remains uncertain.
Screenshots and recordings are selectively edited; the complete conversation, independent dates, identities and outcome are unavailable.
The same-title live EPmR6XOphxY was not locally available. Its 8076-second metadata suggests this 2441-second upload may be an edited excerpt, but clip-level reuse is unresolved.
Sparse visual review does not equal continuous full-video audio-visual review, and the stored sampled images are only 960x540.
